title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 94
paragraphs: These oracles, then, were uttered to them, and the people of Apollonia, keeping it a secret, entrusted certain citizens to handle the matter; and they handled it for them thus. When Euenios was sitting on a seat in public, they came and sat beside him, and conversed about other matters, and at last they came to sympathizing with him in his misfortune; and leading him on in this way, they asked what satisfaction he would choose, if the people of Apollonia should undertake to give him satisfaction for what they had done. He, not having heard the oracle, made his choice and said that if there were given him the lands belonging to certain citizens — naming those he knew to own the two best plots of land in Apollonia — along with a house as well, which he knew to be the best in the city, if he became owner of these, he would have no anger against them in the future, and this satisfaction would be sufficient if given to him. While he was speaking thus, the men sitting beside him interrupted: “Euenios, this is the satisfaction the Apolloniates pay to you for your blinding, in accordance with the oracles given them.” At this he was angry, finding out the whole matter and considering that he had been deceived; but they bought the property from those who owned it and gave him what he had chosen. And immediately after this he had a natural gift of divination, so that he became very famous.
